Best known covering arrays, with evidence

A covering array CA(N; t, k, v) is an N by k array over v symbols in which every choice of t columns shows every one of the vt value combinations in some row. This table records, for each strength t and alphabet size v, the smallest known N for each number of columns k, and says where every entry comes from. The baseline is the November 2024 status of Charles J. Colbourn's covering array tables as preserved by Ulrike Groemping in the CAs R package (tier CITED). Sizes published in papers and not in the snapshot are also tier CITED, each naming its paper (source S7, marked published), until an array is in hand. Entries with an explicit array in hand were checked exhaustively by a verifier and carry the array's SHA-256 and a stamp (tier VERIFIED). Arrays too large to check in full on the public runner were screened on random column windows (tier SCREENED); they are listed but do not count as best known. Where Colbourn's construction for an entry, as checked here, did not give a covering array at the recorded size, the entry stays as recorded and its rung is marked disputed (tier DISPUTED). No entry here is a computed size. Sizes that follow from these entries by published constructions (fusing symbols, deriving a strength, Power CT and others) are recomputed on every change and listed separately, each with its arithmetic, on the derived sizes page (133 points); they are not counted as best known here.

Rows are stair-steps: an entry (t, v, k, N) means N runs suffice for up to k columns, so the best known N at k is the smallest N among entries with at least k columns. The construction column names the construction or search that produced each entry, where it is known. For every array on file, constant rows is the largest number of its rows that can be made constant by permuting symbols within columns, a property that matters when the array is an ingredient of another construction. Anyone can add an array by pull request; see how to submit. The data is table/ in the repository; the raw file table/ca_table.csv is the machine-readable form (see the README for the stair-step rule and an R snippet).

  • table rows 14,581
  • verified rows 779

  • screened rows, not yet verified in full 0
  • disputed entries 3
  • arrays on file 360

Generated 2026-11-01 from table/ca_table.csv and table/MANIFEST.csv.

What the columns of ca_table.csv mean
columnmeaning
t, v, k, Nthe claim: N runs suffice for a covering array of strength t on up to k columns of v symbols (stair-step: the best known N at k is the smallest N among entries with at least k columns)
tierthe evidence class. CITED: traceable to a dated snapshot or publication, no array in hand (the 13,641 baseline rows are Colbourn's tables of November 2024). VERIFIED: an explicit array was checked exhaustively at strength t. SCREENED: an array too large for the public check, screened on random column windows, listed but not counted as best known. FAILED_PENDING_RECHECK: a verification attempt that failed its dimension check, kept and superseded by a later row. DISPUTED (since 2026-10-23): an added row beside a CITED entry whose cited construction, as implemented and checked here, did not give a covering array at the recorded size; the CITED row stays as recorded and is still counted, and the rung is marked disputed
source_idthe source class. S1 Colbourn's tables (the CAs snapshot), S4 NIST covering array library, S5 Dwyer CA_Database, S6 data and constructions of the CAs package, S7 literature and community submissions, S8 arrays built by this project with its own scripts (tools/own_arrays, tools/cphf), verified in full, an array too large to store through its checked certificate (table/certificates)
source_detailthe exact retrieval or generation recipe (URL and commit, or the generating call and package version)
snapshot_idthe dated source: colbourn-2024-11-ug for the baseline, pr-N (or the submission folder name) for a submission, the DOI or the arXiv id with version (for example doi:10.3390/math12121908, arXiv:2510.13122v2) for a paper, empty where source_detail already carries a dated recipe
array_sha256SHA-256 of the array in canonical form (0-based symbols, one run per line), for rows with an array
verify_stampthe verifier, its version or commit, the date and the machine; on this page each stamp links to that verifier (caverify on CRAN, or the ca_verify source at that commit), to the array file or certificate where one is stored, and to the verification log
enteredthe date the row was added
notescomparison with the previous best as of entry, credit, submission, and supersession notes; every construction belongs to the sources the row names, and a row whose construction is this project's own says so
lb, lb_evidencereserved for lower-bound evidence, empty in every row so far
constructionthe construction or search that produced the entry, in a researcher's words; for the baseline it is Colbourn's own label. Where Colbourn's table and a verified array give the same entry, the page shows both, labelled. The Dwyer source codes are Aaron Dwyer's abbreviations for the method; many of his arrays cite personal communication with Colbourn

The full schema is in table/README.md.

Community submissions

One entry per submission, newest first. Open one to see its arrays.
